analysis_notes.evil_domain_observation: The Torah mentions several evil-side entities: קלפות (klipot), רשעים (the wicked), פושעי ישראל (Jewish sinners), משומדים (apostates). However, the Rebbe does not use explicit bechina language for these entities — he describes them functionally and behaviorally. The klipot 'lead' (מוליכין) the wicked 'around' the point — this is narrative description and the verse 'סָבִיב רְשָׁעִים יִתְהַלָּכוּן' is cited as a proof-verse for the behavior, not as a bechina equation. Therefore no evil nodes are flagged for addition to the bechina dataset. If the dataset were to add an evil-domain edge for this Torah, the most defensible candidates would be: קלפות as the force that keeps souls in the circles, and מניעות (obstacles) as the functional manifestation of their action — but these are eitza relationships (the klipot cause the obstacles), not bechina.
analysis_notes.torah_brevity_note: Torah #45 LM2 is an unusually short Torah — only 4 sentences (approx. 300 Hebrew words). Its conceptual structure is correspondingly compact: one central good cluster (Pkg 1: Shabbat/inner-point/Tzaddik) and one structural context cluster (Pkg 2: six-days/circles). The entire teaching serves as an introduction to a longer discussion implied by 'כַּמּוּבָא' at the end.
good_evil_mirror_pairs: Package 1 (Shabbat/inner point/Tzaddik — the holy destination) ↔ the implicit evil domain (klipot/wicked who circle but cannot enter). The Torah describes this polarity explicitly but does not encode the evil side in bechina language.
